ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Wilma Mankiller

code.originalText: Seven-month review: minimal manifestation status, prednisone and pyridostigmine reduction, azathioprine safety, kidney screening, and plans for the year

text.paragraph: Ms. Mankiller returns seven months after her diagnosis. She has had no drooping eyelids, double vision or trouble chewing since the summer; only after a very long day does she feel her arms tire. Prednisone is now 15 mg each morning, and she stopped trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole when the dose fell below 20 mg last week, as planned. She takes azathioprine 150 mg daily; the blood tests at the Cherokee Nation clinic two and six weeks after the dose increase were normal and the nurse called her each time. She has returned to full-time work. She sleeps better on the lower prednisone dose. Home blood pressure readings average 116/74. She drinks about 2.5 liters of water a day and has had no flank pain or blood in the urine. She would like fewer pyridostigmine tablets. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-10-12; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; blood pressure 118/76 mm Hg; weight 63.6 kg
No ptosis after one minute of upgaze; no diplopia
Strength 5 of 5 without fatigue; speech normal

Drooping eyelids and double vision for six weeks, worse in the evening, with fatigable weakness of the arms and neck, tiring when chewing and a nasal voice after long talks; a disorder of the neuromuscular junction suspected
S — Synthetic presenting problem, resolved at the second visit when antibodies and nerve testing established myasthenia gravis.
Generalized myasthenia gravis, acetylcholine receptor antibody positive, MGFA class IIa, without thymoma; synthetic modern detail linked to her documented myasthenia gravis of 1980

S — Synthetic antibody level, electrodiagnosis, class and treatment; the diagnosis less than a year after the crash, and recovery with Cherokee medicine people, surgery and drug therapy, are documented (D).
Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (hereditary, as she has described it), with normal kidney function; to be staged
S — The hereditary polycystic kidney disease is documented (D) from her later public account; its detection before the index date, and every value, are synthetic.
Recovery from major trauma in a head-on car crash last year: fractures of both legs, ribs and face, with many operations; walks independently, with a cane on rough ground
S — The crash, the operations and the injuries are documented (D); the current function is synthetic.
Long-term glucocorticoid therapy for myasthenia gravis, with monitoring of glucose, blood pressure, weight, bone health, mood, sleep, eyes and infection
Azathioprine as steroid-sparing therapy, with blood count and liver test monitoring
Acquired absence of the thymus after robotic extended thymectomy for myasthenia gravis (pathology: thymic follicular hyperplasia, no thymoma)
S — Synthetic: recorded after the thymectomy; the sources name surgery among her treatments without saying which.

list.item: A confirmed diagnosis and treatment plan within three weeks. Outcome by 2026-03-23: AChR antibodies, nerve stimulation, chest CT and kidney ultrasound done; generalized MG diagnosed and treatment begun at two weeks [S]
Minimal manifestation status (MG-ADL 0 to 1) within a year, with prednisone at 7.5 mg or less. Outcome by 2026-10-12: MG-ADL 7 at diagnosis, 1 at seven months; prednisone 15 mg and still tapering [S]

No myasthenic crisis, and she knows the warning signs and the medicines to avoid. Outcome by 2026-10-12: No crisis; FVC 3.25 to 3.62 L; she carries a wallet card and the list of medicines to avoid [S]

Kidney health: eGFR and urine albumin yearly, home blood pressure 110/75 mm Hg or lower if it rises above 130/85, 2 to 3 liters of water a day, and no NSAIDs. Outcome by 2026-10-12: eGFR normal; urine albumin normal; home blood pressure about 116/74 without medicine [S]
Return to full-time work for the Cherokee Nation. Outcome by 2026-10-12: Back at work full time from the seventh month [S]
